Solution 1 is correct. The spectrum is $\{p-1, -(p-1), 1 \,(\times p-1), -1 \,(\times p-1)\}$, which I checked against the Ramanujan sums $c_{2p}(a)$. The amplitudes at $d$ odd, $d\neq p$, are proportional to $\sin\frac{pt}{2}\cos\frac{(p-2)t}{2}$ and at $d$ even, $d\neq 0$, to $\sin\frac{pt}{2}\sin\frac{(p-2)t}{2}$. Both vanish only if $\sin\frac{pt}{2}=0$, so $t=2\pi m/p$. At $m=1$ the state is $\cos t\, e_0 + i\sin t\, e_p$ with $\sin t\neq 0$, which is a genuine fractional revival. For $p=3$ (the 6-cycle), I verified directly that the amplitude at vertex 1 vanishes at $t=2\pi/3$, so $t^*=2\pi/p$.

Solution 2 ($p$) has no derivation behind it. Solution 3 ($2\pi/(p-1)$) uses only the spectral radius and never checks the revival condition. For $p=3$ it gives $t=\pi$, where $\sin(pt/2)=\sin(3\pi/2)\neq 0$, so the walk does not revive in the required sense.

CHOICE: 1
